Implementation Plan

Plan for #6639: add regression tests for the inline-config push bypass (re-issued from #6336)

Planning ref: `main` @ `e4c54adf48f2565188abbcf9292b0e13448492b7`. The planning context recorded `e735f99`; both are on `main` and there's no integration branch, so there's no branch mismatch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends test_per_command_config_push_asks_without_using_origin_prs
Scope-mode justification: The answer to Q1 was A, so this delivers regression tests only. I confirmed the finding no longer reproduces on `main`. In both hook copies, lines 544-546 set `config_override` for any `-c` or `--config-env` option. Lines 1557-1559 then add the reason "per-command Git configuration may redirect the push" and `continue` before `_push_targets` runs. So `--repo=origin main` is never read as a refspec, and the default-branch skip can't happen. I ran the unmodified template hook against a copy of the `merged_branch_repo` fixture (default branch `main`, current branch `feature/x`). All four planned commands returned `(0, '')` with `permissionDecision == "ask"`, never called `query_pull_requests`, and never printed `other/repo`. Changing the decision to deny (option B) would contradict the documented "ask" behaviour in `agents.md`. Leaving the shape untested (option C) is less safe. Pinning the invariant with tests is the complete, smallest change.

Data flow / State machines / Failure modes: not included; this is a tests-only change.

1. Files likely to change
- `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`: this is the only file that changes.

Do not change:
- `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` and `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`. They are byte-identical, which I checked with `cmp`. They are read only here.
- `agents.md`.
- No other test changes.

2. Functions or modules to implement
In `test_per_command_config_push_asks_without_using_origin_prs` (the parametrize list just before the function, currently about lines 1348-1356), add these four entries after the existing seven:
- `"git -c remote.main.url=https://github.com/other/repo -c push.default=current push --repo=origin main"` (the exact exploit shape)
- `"git -c push.default=current push --repo=origin main"`
- `"git -cremote.main.url=https://github.com/other/repo push --repo origin main"`
- `"git --config-env=remote.main.url=REMOTE_URL push --repo=origin main"`

Keep the literal `main`. The fixture runs `git init -b main` and points `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` at `origin/main`, so `main` is the default branch and the default-branch skip the finding describes is actually exercised.

Keep the test body and its three assertions unchanged:
- `code == 0 and message == ""`
- the last output line's `permissionDecision == "ask"`
- `"other/repo" not in output`

Also keep the `query_pull_requests` monkeypatch that calls `pytest.fail`.

Optionally, add a comment line above the new entries: `# #6336/#6639 exploit shape: inline remote + --repo with the default branch as positional.`

3. Data structures affected: none.

4. API or interface changes: none. Hook behaviour, log output and permission decisions don't change.

## Decisions

### D1 — Pin the exploit with regression tests instead of changing the guard
- Chosen: add four parametrize entries to the existing inline-config push test, with no hook change.
- Alternatives considered:
  - Hard-deny inline-config pushes (option B), which changes both hooks, `agents.md` and the existing "ask" tests.
  - Close the finding with no change (option C).
  - Write a new dedicated test function.
- Why: The bypass is already closed by the `config_override` short-circuit, as confirmed above. The Q1 answer (A) asks for tests only. Extending the existing parametrized test reuses its fixture and assertions instead of duplicating them.

### D2 — Keep the literal `main` positional
- Chosen: use `main` unchanged in all four commands.
- Alternatives considered: read the default branch dynamically from the fixture.
- Why: The `merged_branch_repo` fixture hard-codes `main` as the default branch, so the literal exercises the default-branch path the finding describes.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: the interactive merged-PR guard hook, which sits between a model-issued Bash command and `git push`. The tests pin that per-command Git configuration (`-c`, `-c<key>`, `--config-env`) never lets origin's PR history authorize a push, and that the user must confirm every such push.
- Authorization: no new endpoint or other exposed surface.
- External input: the test commands use the non-secret placeholder URL `https://github.com/other/repo` and the env-var name `REMOTE_URL`. The existing `"other/repo" not in output` assertion keeps the rule that config values (which may contain credentials) are never printed.
- Abuse cases covered:
  - The finding's exact command, which spoofs `remote.main.url`, sets `push.default=current`, and passes the default branch as a positional to `--repo`.
  - The same command without a URL override.
  - The glued `-c` form.
  - The `--config-env` form.

5. Risks and edge cases
- The tests pin the outcome (ask, no PR query), not which code path produced it. In my probe, the control command without config, `git push --repo=origin main`, also returned "ask". So if the `config_override` short-circuit were removed, another rule might still produce "ask" and the test would keep passing.
  - The implementer may tighten this by also asserting `"per-command Git configuration" in output` for the new cases, but only after checking that the hook prints that reason text. If it doesn't, don't add the assertion.
- Live/template parity: no hook edit, so `tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py` and the byte-identity tests are unaffected.
- Changelog: this is a tests-only change with no user-visible behaviour change. I'm assuming no `changelog.d/` fragment is needed under CLAUDE.md §20. If the implementer reads §20 differently, add a one-line fragment `changelog.d/6639-merged-pr-guard-inline-config-tests.md`.
- PR body:
  - Use `Fixes #6639`.
  - Say the finding was verified fixed on `main` by PR #6286's guard changes.
  - Reference tracker #3576 only with `Refs #3576`, never a closing keyword (§21).
  - Run `scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py` on the body first.

6. Testing considerations
- Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py -k per_command_config_push`. Expect 11 passing cases (7 existing plus 4 new).
- Run the whole file, plus `tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py`, to confirm nothing else regressed.
- pytest isn't installed in the planning sandbox, so I couldn't run pytest here. The plain-Python probe of the unmodified template hook against the fixture setup showed the expected results for all four commands. Treat pytest results as unverified until CI runs (CI job `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`).

7. Pre-execution self-check
- Requirements map to the Q1 = A answer: tests only, the exploit command plus `--repo=origin <default-branch>` variants, assert ask with no PR query, no hook change.
- I checked these facts in this session: the test and fixture lines, hook lines 544-546 and 1557-1559, live/template byte identity, the fixture's default branch, and the probe results.
- No new identifiers are introduced; only parametrize strings are added.
- No external inputs or credentials are needed.
- The sandbox worktree already had unrelated modified and untracked files (`scripts/ai_engine.sh`, `scripts/clarify_openrouter_broker.py`, `scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py`, `scripts/claude_engine.py`, `workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md`) before planning. The implementer must not include them. The temporary probe file I created under `tests/` was deleted before `git status` ran, which confirmed it was gone.

PLAN_SELF_CHECK: WARNING: The new cases pin the "ask" outcome, but the control `git push --repo=origin main` also asks, so they don't uniquely pin the config_override path; optionally also assert the per-command-config reason text after checking that the hook prints it.
